posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
There we go. The first pony has crossed the finish line. Hit the showers, Omnitron-X, we’ll call you when it’s time for you to receive your medal.

Citizen Dawn in the Tim Cataclysm versus the Naturalist, Ra, and Omnitron-X. She won the first time, but I accidentally put too many citizens in play during setup so that may have been my fault. Second time, a magic crocigator, a god, and a Terminator messed her up. X was actually the least useful character–his biggest contribution was blowing up environment cards with that eye-beam of his–but Steve Irwin and Carter Hall really pounded the damage down. I honestly have to award MVP to an environment triceratops, though, who was extremely helpful about mowing down citizens for me so the other two could focus on their business.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I swear to god I love the frigging Sentinels.

Plague Rat went to the Final Wasteland to hunt down Chrono-Ranger, who was actually in the past hunting Plague Rat so they just missed each other. Instead, the rat found the Sentinels, Dark Visionary, Tachyon, and Engine of War Bunker. I was worried that the Sentinels wouldn’t last, but their constant teamwork (Sentinel Tactics and Hippocratic Oath both got out in the first round) ensured that they’d always be capable of both inflicting damage and healing. Dark Visionary was far and away the most important member of the team, though, using a combination of her base power, Precognition, and Suggestion to make sure Plague Rat only ever got to play useless ongoing cards that either she, Tachyon, or the Engine of War would destroy.* Tachyon was the biggest damage dealer due strictly to her late-game Lightspeed Barrages, but the Engine of War pounded away pretty hard first with a Flak Cannon, then with a Grenade Launcher when one would become relevant, and after round four with both thanks to a Turret Mode. The environment spat out a few monsters that didn’t impress anyone and were destroyed quickly by barrages of telekinetic force and heavy artillery.

The game was over in eight rounds. All the heroes were down by a maximum of nine HP.

*Technically not true. He did get out one Tooth and Claw, but Tachyon made it completely useless with a Hypersonic Assault the round before, so as far as I’m concerned, the only card he played during that round was an Infection Dark Visionary destroyed before it could even affect the Engine of War.

posts.name: Azqa
posts.cooked: After two failed attempts to save The Dreamer from succumbing to whatever the Treacherous Ape is trying to get her to do (according to conversations elsewhere on this forum) in Megalopolis, the team of Parse, Absolute Zero, Setback, and the Scholar had better luck in the universe where the little girl was roused from slumber while on a tour of the Freedom Tower.  Sadly for Setback, he was in the wrong place at the wrong time when there were two Entry Points and a Dark Hero active and got overloaded with psychic damage, but that did allow Absolute Zero to take out the last two projections needed to save a young girl from her own nightmares.

posts.name: KainNived
posts.cooked:
After getting stomped into the ground by Iron Legacy a few times I decided to change tack and make myself feel better by beating up gloomy.

Seems a cult following for him had sprung up in The Block of all places.  Rook City Wraith, Dark Watch Expatriette, a time displaced and confused Engine of War Bunker, and Dark Watch Mister Fixer showed up to sort things out.

I initially thought it was going to be a real quick game as the Drum and Book pulled in the first rounds.  Set ups went fairly well for everyone but Bunker, couldn't pull any power cards so he mainly functioned as Dark Watch Mister Fixer's ammo tank.  After the first two relics dropped I got nervous that Vast Following would pull, so everyone started unloading on Gloomy.  Classic throwing knives, razor ordnance, micro on Wraith.  Shotty with speed loading and a hollow point/shock round rotation going on DW Expatriette.  Gattling Gun and Flak Cannon on Bunker.  Grease monkey fist and dual crowbars on Fixer... Holy crap can he lay down punishment like that if properly supported.  Bloody knuckles, overdrive, charge all saw use in the last few rounds too.

The pouch did pull eventually.  On the last round.  Gloomy only had 7 hp.  Buuut as Wraith could do 8 damage to it, and Expat 6, EoW 5, and Fixer could do 9 (charge, plus monkey and crowbars) I decided to go ahead and take the relic win...  Just cause.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Skinwalker Gloomweaver rose from one of the corpses in the morgue of the Block, but didn’t realize the pocket dimension would contain his newly corporeal form long enough for a group of heroes to mount an offensive. Fittingly, it was Fanatic who led the charge against the Qlippothic monstrosity; Dark Watch Mr. Fixer, the Sentinels, and Haka were all on hand to join the fight.

It was frigging grueling. Twenty-one bloody damned rounds, and I blame every last one of them on Dark Watch Mr. Fixer. Haka and Fanatic were both knocked down to the absolute minimum possible efficiency as each one had to spend at least one round in two crapping out some card to sacrifice to Bitter Strike; I exempted the Sentinels from this because they don’t have that many cards and needed every one they could pull. It took ten rounds to flip Gloomweaver, and would have taken longer if Fixer’s first card hadn’t been Riveting Crane Style, his second hadn’t been Jack Handle, and his third hadn’t been Harmony. His ability to hit all enemies simultaneously and knock any DR off them was key enough to compensate for how much he reduced Fanatic and Haka to a crawl. The round before Gloomweaver flipped, Fanatic got out her Zealous Offense, which put an even greater burden on Haka to be the one to sacrifice his cards to Mr. Fixer’s blind rage since she couldn’t afford to lose Absolution or Zealous Offense if she wanted to keep Gloomweaver from destroying everyone, but he got by, and Fanatic eventually started getting out a few cards here and there to help; a Sacrosanct Martyr, an Undaunted, whatever.

The Sentinels were the steadiest source of damage, but they didn’t get out Sentinel Tactics until he’d flipped, so a lot of their early damage was stunted by being required to spend their power phase on Mainstay armoring them all. Haka got out a Taiaha fairly early and didn’t have to sacrifice it until he got a spare in his hand, so he was reliably inflicting three points of damage to two targets pretty much all the time.

The inmates in the Block never inflicted any damage. They were either destroyed by a Jack Handle as soon as they got into play, were shot down by agents, or were prevented form inflicting damage by the various cards in the hero decks that prevent bad guys from doing damage.

At the end of the game, thanks to an early play of Hippocratic Oath, the Sentinels were all at max HP, and the rest of the team was in the high teens, save of course for Fanatic, who’d been spamming Sacrosanct Martyr to inflict maximum damage on the zombie-god. I like to think that holy light shattered his spirit beyond reconstruction, but he’s a villain and they seem to have Get Out Of Oblivion Free passes, so probably not.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Setback, the Scholar, Expatriette, and Tempest all got shockingly lucky against Cosmitron in Freedom Tower. I was sure I was gonna die in round three when both Electro-whatever gates came out, but concentrated pouring-on of damage knocked it down to only sixteen HP of damage to everyone, and by then the Scholar had Mortal Form to Energy in play, Tempest had Cleansing Downpour, and Setback had no offense but three cards in hand that would heal the entire party; so everyone was healing back 4 HP per round for three rounds (more when the Scholar got out that one that heals everyone). I was actually being real careful not to inflict too much damage on Cosmitron himself because the only components he had in play were those wussy railguns and I was happier with them in play than a potential army of frigging drones as might happen if he flipped.

Around round ten, the Freedom Tower card that deals everyone 2 HP of cold came out just after Setback had put out the one that lets him absorb and/or redirect damage dealt to other heroes, and he had a good store of unlucky tokens stockpiled, so Cosmitron was taking 8 HP per round from that card (by my reading, Setback still has to suffer damage that targets him and he can’t redirect that; am I wrong?). That helped a lot. Setback was down to 3 HP at the end, but everyone else was at least in the teens when Expatriette played her final Unload with a shotgun, an Uzi, a pistol, and some flaming ammo in one of them to blow the robot apart once and for all.

With Cosmitron reduced to so much crackling rubble, the heroes then all went to find Unity and kick her ass for her, because her Playground came into play and turned all ongoing cards into equipment cards exactly before Cosmitron destroyed all equipment cards. It wasn’t really her fault, but it wasn’t really not her fault either, so I don’t want to hear anyone complaining about fairness.

Completely unrelated to the game I just played, I wonder if the upcoming character Captain Cosmic’s nemesis will be the currently unnamed jerk who decided to power up Cosmitron.

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
JimB:

by my reading, Setback still has to suffer damage that targets him and he can't redirect that; am I wrong?

The only requirement is a hero target, Setback is a hero target, so he can redirect his damage aswell.

posts.name: KainNived
posts.cooked:
One should never be surprised when they run into The Ennead at The Tomb of Anubis.  Least of all the paranormal investigator Faye Diamond, the Dark Watch member known as Nightmist.  She was however surprised when the ritual performed by the Ennead tore open a hole in the fabric of spacetime and she recieved help from those thrilling heroes of yesteryear America's Greatest Legacy and G.I. Bunker!

The only members of the Ennead that made it out to play were Nephthys, Geb, and Tefnut, none of the others got a chance to come out to play.  Bunker got his grenade launcher out early, and with Greatest Legacy's support he was able to lob a ridiculous amount of grenades at the egyptians.  Throw in some inspiration, the flak cannon, and turret mode and the vintage artillery fell like rain. 

DW Nightmist meanwhile managed to play lockdown on the villain deck, while they did get a few cards out they never got another of their ilk out to play. 

The environment helped out as well dropping several trials that beat the Ennead as badly as the heroes.   In the final environment turn The Lord of the Underworld Anubis made his grand entrance, just in time to collect Nephthys personally when G.I. Bunker Flak Cannoned her to death.

The heroes never didn't get to recover any artifacts, none the less Faye considered the expedidtion a success.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Wanting to finish off the Scholar just because seeing those black lines makes me feel as if we’re progressing, I threw him against the Chairman when a thought occurred to me: when I started playing this game, I only played three characters at a time because that’s all my space can afford. It wasn’t until I decided to start wiping Vengeance Five games off the map that I cleared a big ol’ space off the living room floor, arranged things in a circle around me, and hunkered down in the center. Now that I know I have room for five heroes, why not try five heroes against the Chairman, since almost nothing in his deck scales with hero numbers, and see if that doesn’t work?

Well, it worked. It worked fast. Six rounds and he was down, after flipping at the start of the third. Team Leader Tachyon kept everyone drowning in cards; Unity was lucky enough to get out Swift Bot and a Platform Bot in the first round; Freedom Tempest had roughly two third of his deck in hand at the end of the game when his first play was Localized Hurricane that just wiped out the mooks; Absolute Zero almost didn’t even have time to get his setup in play but did manage to Impale the Operative in the first round; and the Scholar…well, actually, the Scholar didn’t have anything to do. The Chairman’s first card was “Rook City Is Mine!” which put Mission Control in play, so since the Scholar had no good cards in hand his first play was Know When to Hold Fast, and then Mission Control put Know When to Turn Loose into play. I didn’t mind hitting the Operative for 9 HP, but it sucked not having any cards in his hand.

Oh, well. The Chairman learned a valuable lesson about trying to acquire superhero real estate when they’re home and have something to say about it.

posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked: Mission Control CAN'T put Turn Loose into play. It discards one-shots.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
McBehrer:

Mission Control CAN’T put Turn Loose into play. It discards one-shots.

Aw, crap. Well, I better go delete the records, then.

posts.name: LevelUpLeo
posts.cooked:
Just played a game solo controlling 3 characters. Chrono-Ranger, Legacy and Ra fighting Ambuscade on the Wagner Mars Base.

 

Man this was easy, but still long for some reason. I felt like I was getting all the right cards and started getting my equipment pretty early. Even an early Countdown didn't hinder me. For example, Ambuscade had his explosive launcher out, but soon enough Ra got a card that made everyone immune to fire. A couple of bounties on Ambuscade and a "Hunter and the Hunted" and Chrono-Ranger became the one taking care of everything coming out. Legacy just had all the right equipment and took most of the damage whenever possible, especially for Chrono-Ranger (instead of having it increased by Hunter and Hunted, it was decreased). Really, the biggest problem was the environment making me discard cards constantly.

 

Actually, upon thinking about it, I should have won sooner. I forgot Galvanize a bunch of time and that due to a few of the bounties, Ambuscade was taking more damage than others... Regardless, its 2 more down for Ansel Moreau.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
JimB:

Aw, crap. Well, I better go delete the records, then.

I did it right this time, no accidental cheating that I know of, and it was still almost play by play exactly the same as the first time I tried putting Team Leader Tachyon, Unity, Freedom Tempest, Absolute Zero, and the Scholar against the Chairman. Tachyon was probably the reason everyone won, since the other four are all desperately dependent on getting cards into hand, but a big part of the play was Cleansing Downpour to keep Unity’s bots alive and to hit the Scholar with two Mortal Form to Energy cards in play so he was zapping back 4 HP per round, while an early draw of Frost’s Cryo-Chamber meant playing Null-point Calibration Suit early on left Absolute Zero tanking villains who really couldn’t hurt him much faster than he was healing.

posts.name: KainNived
posts.cooked:
While reading a weathered copy of The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire in the far off wastes of the far future the Eternal Haka was surprised to find a time rift opening in front of him. It had been decades since the last one. He considered it good to take a walk about in the time stream now and again, one gets to be around people again, a chance to see old friends possibly, pick up some more books, and maybe even a cupcake if the time was right. Thus he walked through the time portal to find himself on an old familiar battle ground sadly bereft of cupcakes. The pike industrial complex, where he heard a villain monologuing.

It was Kismet, standing across from her ready for battle were two members of Darkwatch, Nightmist and Expatriette, as well as Rook City’s own Wraith! One would have thought the villainess’s unnatural luck would have kept an additional opponant away, but time has a way of evening out luck. Perhaps that’s why it had to come from so far.

Things went pretty simply. Set ups were fast. Expat had Pride in the starting hand and quick draw so she was able to bring the heat. Haka also therw down punishment and managed to keep himself healed. Wraith played deck manipulation which kept Kismet in check and kept the rats from mutating. DW Nightmist was able with the neckless and deck stacking to keep blasting Kismet’s ongoings and occasionally deal damage while healing herself.

That just leaves 4 base set heroes left to face Kismet! So by all means someone take her out!

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Because I am arrogant and stupid, I wanted to get as many slots cleared off as I could. Only six heroes left hadn’t fought any of the Vengeance Five yet, so of them I picked Engine of War Bunker, KNYFE, Dark Watch Mister Fixer, the Sentinels, and Dark Watch Setback (the last choice was agonizing, but between him and Parse, I figured I needed more HP to soak up the hits). The five of them boarded the Mobile Defense Platform, figuring it would just be Baron Blade pulling his usual Bizarro-Murphy-from-Sealab-2021 shtick,* but instead there was a bloody damned army of villains in there that the team was, frankly, woefully unprepared for. The Engine of War was pretty useless; after destroying a couple of enemy ongoings, he didn’t get a weapon car in hand for almost six rounds and was lucky to get a few External Combustions he could use. KNYFE was slightly better, though her first two cards were party-damaging Incidental Contacts because she too couldn’t get any equipment in hand until the end of round two. Mister Fixer tried to keep putting his own style cards in play to sacrifice for punches, but he did end up having to dip into Bunker’s Ammo Drop for the sake of keeping his own Dual Crowbars in play; the Sentinels were, as usual, MVPs with a fairly early play of Sentinel Tactics combined with some lucky draws of their various “damage everyone, or at least more than one person” cards to keep them going at a good clip. Dark Watch Setback contributed slightly more than the Engine of War did, mostly by putting out useless ongoings to sacrifice to either Mister Fixer or Ermine (whom I will hate forever), though he did get off some very well-timed Exceeded Expectations to wipe out his unlucky pool before playing a previously suicidal Cause and Effect.

The Vengeance Five were screwed by, paradoxically, a lucky draw. At the start of round one, Baron Blade helped Proletariat get four clones into play, so of course the heroes pounded on him as hard as they could to make sure he’d finish himself off in round two with his own psychic damage. He put out ten HP of damage in round one, but killed himself off in round two. After that, it was a matter of focusing on whoever was screwing the group more (looking at you, Revenant) or whose death would screw the party least (looking at you, Ermine), and just hoping to get good cards in hand.

Around round six, Writhe was the hero with the most HP left (he had 13) and I finally got Caliginous Form into play, nearly immunizing the entire party from damage. Since everyone else had in the neighborhood of six to eight, that was extremely important. In round nine, the villains were defeated. I’d been delaying killing Friction for as long as possible because when Dark Watch Mister Fixer is in your group, you don’t need anyone’s help wiping out the party’s setup, so a final play of Horrifying Dichotomy wiped her and the Baron out in a single blow.

Sparks: Why would we want to blow up the Earth, where we are right now?
Bizarro Murphy: Because it is…BIZARRO!
Sparks: It’s STUPID.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: I will never understand why anyone, supervillains or otherwise, would have any interest in Insula Primalis, but the Vengeance Five did, so Fanatic, Parse, Unity, Haka, and Wraith decided to go stop them because no one needs an army of villains with mind-controlled cyborg dinosaurs or whatever they were actually planning to do. It was a tough fight made easier by a friendly Tyrannosaurus Rex, and by Parse getting Swift Bot and Stealth Bot out for Unity in the first round (I never stop thinking it’s funny when Unity gets to play a bot without having to sacrifice anything), the latter of which was able to absorb a whole lot of damage for the party. Haka was damage guy, as you’d expect, and Proletariat was the first to go down, as you’d also expect. I don’t know whom to award MVP to, but let’s say Unity for her army of bots countering the army of villains and and giving Fanatic a cyber-arm with which to zap-punch villains.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Niece and I playing a game.  (Her 2nd or 3rd time playing.)  Eternal Haka (her), Scholar (her), Naturalist (me), and Absolute Zero (me) verses Advanced Baron Blade on a Mobile Defense Platform.

Due to initial slow damage ramp-up Blade got 15 cards into his discard pile the round we flipped him.  Very few Hasten Dooms, and he played Blade Battalions a lot it seemed.  Niece had fun running Scholar - who mainly tanked damage with Iron Form and played support cards.  Haka got a few weapons out and pounded on stuff - and niece didn't quite finish off Blade with a 10-point Haka of Battle play.  Absolute Zero got his modules and a Focused Apecture out early and did a fair amount of damage.  The Naturalist did a fairly simple play and stayed in Crocodile form most of the game to nom on Blade and his minions. 

The Environment Deck did not really do much.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Baron Blade, Friction, Fright Train, and Proletariat got together in Rook City to try to free their pal Ermine from state prison where she was serving time for being a generally awful person. Nightmist, Setback, Golem Unity, and Ra were on hand to stop them. During the first round, after Nightmist unleashed the most powerful portal possible to the darkness beyond time on all enemies, after Setback pounded on Proletariat’s head, after Ra used his fire to burn the collective villain, Fright Train’s rampage critically weakened the support structures of an old cathedral Proletariat was standing near, causing a gargoyle to fall on the Russian villain’s head, killing him.

Nothing else I can say about this match compares to that. That is all the information worth imparting. All the heroes lived, and all the villains lost, but that is of strictly secondary value to the fact that Proletariat basically died because Bugs Bunny dropped an anvil on his head.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
My god. I think I’m done with this game for a while.

Grand Warlord Voss in the randomly chosen Tomb of Anubis vs. more or less randomly chosen Price of Freedom Wraith, Eternal Haka, Bunker, and Nightmist. Voss’s setup cards are one Gene-Bound Frosthound, two Gene-Bound Psi-Weavers, and one Gene-Bound Shock Infantry; his first draw is TCF Conqueror. First round, every hero has taken at least 9 HP.

Wraith plays Throwing Knives and plinks away. Haka plays Ground Pound, thank god. Bunker plays Grenade Launcher and plinks away, finishing off a Psi-Weaver. Nightmist has nothing good in her hand, so she plays Heedless Lash and puts Mist Form into play, which she just does to have something to sacrifice to the warship. Luck of luck, one of the two cards she draws is her Amulet of the Elder Gods.

Shamise comes out of the environment. “Okay,” I think, “I can deal with this.”

Playing two cards because of his warship, Voss plays a Gene-Bound Guard and Field Lieutenant Tamar. All villain targets save for the warship have DR 2; Wraith and Bunker cannot hurt them. I begin to cry very softly to myself, but carrying on is really my only choice, so Wraith plays a Utility Belt to inflict two whole points of damage to Shamise. Haka plays Taiaha and knocks Shamise for three, then the Gene-Bound Guard for one. Bunker plays his Gatling Gun and inflicts one whole point of damage to the warship and two to Shamise, finishing him off. Wraith takes the Rod of Anubis for the sake of having something to hit with. Nightmist plays her Amulet, then damages herself with Investigation for the sake of bouncing it back as one point of damage to the Guard.

Judgement of Anubis comes out, hurting the whole team but luckily finishing off that damned guard so one point of the two points of damage can leak through to the minions. There’s no stopping the hail of damage coming out, though, and Wraith loses her Utility Belt. Everyone is down to about 11 HP.

Wraith has zero effective damage potential, so she plays Infrared Eyepiece to at least bury one more Gene-bound Guard. The minions have to go, so the party grits their teeth and take it as Haka plays Rampage, wiping out the minions and taking a lot of punishment from Anubis for it. His Taiaha finishes off the lieutenant and takes a chunk out of Anubis, though a bit late. Bunker focuses fire on the warship, finally killing it, and getting out some Heavy Plating a bit late to be useful. Nightmist plays another Heedless Lash and bounces the damage at Anubis, and putting a useless Scouring Mists into her hand.

A Swarm of Scarabs come out and I curse every known deity, then make a few up to curse them too. Voss flips and gets a Forced Deployment because of course he does. Wraith tosses out another Utility Belt and starts chucking knives and zapping Voss for an overwhelming three HP. Haka puts out Ta Moko and finishes off Anubis, then wallops Voss, who is not amused. Bunker shoots the alien warlord twice, plays Auxiliary Power Source because what else is he doing with these cards, and passes to Nightmist, who plays Planar Banishment to get rid of the Swinging Blades and the Forced Deployment. A few tons of minions come out, none of whom Nightmist is capable of damaging any longer, so she draws her card and hopes for the best.

Mdjai comes out to ping all the heroes, which annoys me.

When Voss’s turn comes, the damage Nightmist inflicted to herself with her early spells is enough that the rush of minions wipe her out. The rest of the group is anywhere between four and one HP. It seems like game over, but I am stubborn, and I have an ace up my sleeve: Wraith’s Smoke Bombs. Almost any damage anyone would inflict should be reduced to nothing by them. She has nothing useful to do now, so she halfheartedly zaps Mdjai with the Rod of Anubis and peeks at Voss’s deck. Haka plays Punish the Weak and can now inflict three points of damage to a minion, which he uses to wipe out the Gene-Bound Guard first and that Gene-Bound Shock Infantry Next. Bunker shoots as many people as he can. Nightmist’s ghost uses some mojo to heal Wraith up to 2 HP in case something happens.

It carries on like that for four more rounds, with damage being diverted to armored targets and reduced down to nothing so the whole group is at no higher than 4 HP at any time. Wraith gets out a Stun Gun eventually but can’t penetrate Voss’s armor for two rounds until she finally gets a Micro-Targeting Computer and can stun him to the point that he can no longer damage anyone very much and Nightmist’s ghost keeps healing as best she can. In the final round, Voss pulls out another Forced Deployment and, with 24 HP left, that’s pretty much game over. It is not physically possible to deal that much damage with the cards I have, so all I can do is play and hope for the best.

Wraith plays a second Infrared Eyepiece because there’s nothing else to do. This brings her up to eight pieces of equipment in play. She hits Voss for 6 HP with a Throwing Knife and a Stun Gun, and draws an Inventory Barrage.

One of Nightmist’s incapacitated powers is to allow a player to play a card. If Wraith plays that, she’ll inflict up to 16 points of damage. Haka only needs to hit for 2 to finish the game.

So, with Wraith at 1 HP, Haka at 4, and Bunker at 2, the heroes manage to kick the alien out of the Tomb of Anubis.

I should feel exhilarated, and maybe I will tomorrow, but for right now? Yeah, enough is enough.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: I wanted just a quick game, so Dark Watch Mr. Fixer and Haka just beat up Miss Information in the Time Cataclysm. So did Dark Watch Expatriette, but only because I misread the chart. Oh, well.

posts.name: Azqa
posts.cooked:
I probably played this horribly, considering how things ended, but...the Dreamer decided to throw a psychic tantrum in the middle of Pike Industrial Complex.  Rats and vats are great playmates.  Legacy, Bunker, Chrono-Ranger and Nightmist sought to prevent things from getting out of hand.

Between Legacy's galvanizing presence, the damage of the other three, and an early chemical explosion of a supercooled trisolvent vat, the projections were gone by the end of the second turn and the Dreamer flipped.  Since the only ongoing in play was Danger Sense, I didn't think it was going to be too bad.  A few turns later, the heroes were down around 5 health, and Nightmist went into Mistform with a Starshield necklace to heal up and build up a bit.  Chrono-ranger bit the dust and I probably shouldn't have tried to manage the flood of projections with only Legacy and Bunker, but eventually things degraded into the projections shaking their fists at the mist while escaped lab rats chewed futilely at those same projections who were strengthened by the presence of two dark heroes and the other three heroes played the waiting game from the ground.  Eventually, two mutagens let the four rats actually take down a treacherous ape and tooth fairy to get the last two projections under the Dreamer's character card and...the day was saved?  It felt like a very bizarre way to succeed.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Plague Rat was causing trouble in the Realm of Discord. I don’t know how it happened, but since Dark Watch Mr. Fixer, Dark Watch Expatriette, and Dark Watch Setback were involved in chasing him down, I will assume Dark Watch Nightmist had something to do with it. The Dark Watch also invited the Argent Adept along, I guess to bolster their suddenly lacking magical might.

I have to say, I have been pretty vocal about disliking the Argent Adept, but in this fight he was key, all thanks to a lucky draw: his first three cards were Rhapsody of Vigor, Sarabande of Destruction, and Drake’s Pipes. With those in play, he was able to keep the party healthy, completely hobble Plague Rat’s Infections and/or the environment deck (first two cards out of it were Portal Fiends, so it was nice that the Adept was able to just make them go bye-bye), and was just in general the main reason everyone survived. Of course Setback was there primarily to give cards to Mr. Fixer’s Bitter Strike, though to be fair Mr. Fixer only cannibalized the team’s equipment when it was necessary to keep his own Driving Mantis out. Expatriette’s first play was an Arsenal Access, which revealed a Tactical Shotgun and an Assault Rifle; an agonizing choice, but I had to go for the shotgun. Plague Rat did not appreciate its effects as it was blasted into his face every round for seven rounds, and she was maybe the single biggest contributor of damage.

In retrospect, I wish I had let Mr. Fixer get infected so he could keep redirecting the damage back to Plague Rat. Ah well, live and learn.

I’ve played…well, I don’t know how many games with Dark Watch Setback now, but you can go to the Google document and count if you’re curious. I just have not figured out what to do with him. He is crippled by the loss of his power to add unlucky tokens to his pool, forcing him–and me–to wait endlessly for a card that will add rather than rely on removals, and I don’t want to derail the thread, but if anyone has an idea of what to do with him, I’d love a private message.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Another Miss Information in the Block. GI Bunker, Ra, Dark Watch Nightmist. Ra fell, which is the first time any hero has ever been incapacitated by Miss Information before. I guess it was bound to happen sooner or later, though. It took six rounds to get her to flip, and inmates were whaling on him without the defenses Bunker or Nightmist could erect, and he couldn’t draw a staff to get for HP, and that was that. The heroes still won, and good for them, but still, I don’t know what to make of Miss Information actually incapacitating a hero. My world view is shattered.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Just two games left each for Chrono-Ranger and the Naturalist, both of whom were on hand along with the Argent Adept and Unity to beat the crap out of Bomber Blade in the Freedom Tower, who learned it just plain doesn’t matter how many bombs you set if you’re the only target to aim at at Unity has the chance to put out a Turret Bot and two Platform Bots. The bots might not have lasted as long had Chrono-Ranger not been sedating Blade at every opportunity, but still, five rounds and out. The only hard part of it was figuring out which cards to sacrifice to Devious Disruptions.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Chrono-Ranger and Parse are both very good against Grand Warlord Voss. You just keep your portals and your spaceships and whatever to yourself, sir, while my ally makes everything we do hurt you more. Then Nightmist will sit there with her chin tilted forward, begging, “C’mon, hit me, what are you, a wussy or something? My necklace? Don’t worry about that necklace, just hit me, puss,” and Golem Unity’s bots will wreck your onslaught while absorbing a lot of punishment.

Seriously, after you’ve tried to punch Nightmist three times and each time that damage has bounced back at you, I feel like everything that happens to you from there on out is your own fault.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: In my quest to clear some heroes off the board, I just threw the Naturalist, Elemental Wrath Absolute Zero, Mister Fixer, and Price of Freedom Wraith against Plague Rat in the Ruins of Atlantis. It took a while because none of them are heavy hitters…or at least, the Naturalist wasn’t, because he spent all time in rhino form with Resilient Hide out so Wraith’s Smoke Bombs would more or less immunize the whole team from damage. His bigger cards could still break through, of course, but preventing all that damage…tasty.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
A storm just knocked out my power for half an hour as well as the record of an absolutely cataclysmic beating Chrono-Ranger, Fanatic, KNYFE, and Price of Freedom Wraith laid on Spite, Agent of Gloom. As best I remember it:

The first victim played was a Lost Child, and the first card played was an Innocent Bystander, so the team was able to flip his drug, “Mynd-Phyre,” before it even had a chance to do anything. Chrono-Ranger’s first play was a double-play of Eye on the Prize and “By Any Means,” so everyone was doing plenty of damage right from the start, except for Wraith, whose Infrared Eyepiece made sure Spite only drew the cards the heroes allowed him to. Chrono-Ranger got out a Compounded Bow in round two, so he and Fanatic were both putting out at least 5 HP per round, and KNYFE, with her Prototype Servo-Gauntlet and her two Battlefield Experiences, was generally doing more. Chrono-Ranger’s third and final card was “the Ultimate Target,” but it barely had a chance to matter; Wraith, with a combination of of Utility Belt, Razor Ordinance, Micro-Targeting Computer, and Stun Bolt finished off his final 10 HP with something to spare before the environment phase.

I am immensely pleased that Chrono-Ranger’s final event in this marathon should be one he can hold his head high from.

posts.name: Rabk
posts.cooked:
Trying to whittle a few more off of the list: 

  1. [Extra-]Advanced Voss attempted to invade the Final Wasteland, but was thwarted by Dark Watch Expat, Argent Adept, Tachyon, and EOW Bunker. It was hardly a contest at all.  Mr. Graves, sitting first in turn order, had all of Voss' nasty plays covered with ease. Both times that a Forced Deployment came out the man in the suit was waiting with a mode card in hand to destroy it and was then so inspired by AA that he dropped External Combustions on both resultant swarms of minions. A loaded Omni-Cannon fired from turret mode also made short work of the dreadnaught.
  2. The young Vanessa Long was found dreaming her horrid dreams in the Time Cataclysm by Redeemer Fanatic, GI Bunker, and Young Legacy. Between =3 and their massive damage output, they quickly cut those pesky nightmares down to size. At the end of the third round they had Inspiring Presence, Embolden, and Sacrosant Martyr all sitting on the table -- none of the baddies really hung for around for long after that.
  3. Akash'buta dared to show her face in Rook City and was promptly Taken Down by Legacy, Wraith, Nightmist, and Setback... Just look at that team. Look at it. I don't think I even need to describe the beating that poor goddess took. She didn't help herself any when she discarded some of the scariest cards in Rook City while letting both the private eye and the good doctor come into play, either.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Over the weekend, I tried…five, maybe six times to throw Dark Watch Mister Fixer, Dark Watch Expatriette, Dark Watch Setback, and the Naturalist against Iron Legacy, in an effort to get the Naturalist finished. None of the attempts worked. Every attempt sucked. Every part of every attempt sucked, and I eventually realized the only way it would work is if Expatriette got an RPG Launcher and the Naturalist got Crafty Assault both in their first draws, which was statistically inevitable but grueling to consider. Tonight, I rolled more or less randomly (the Naturalist was picked deliberately, of course), ending up with Golem Unity, Dark Watch Expatriette, Price of Freedom Wraith, and the Naturalist against Iron Prick. I was about half boned from the start when three of his four starting ongoings were Demoralizing Presence, Armored Fortitude, and Armored Fortitude; but his last one was the fairly useless Superhuman Redirection, and his first draw was another, so I decided to stick with it, not least because one of Wraith’s hand was an Infrared Eyepiece.

Unity got out a Bee Bot in the first and second rounds, and Expatriette played an RPG Launcher in the second, knocking first his damage buffs off and then taking down his armor enough to bother with hitting him. Wraith took only three rounds to get out her Infrared Eyepiece + Utility Belt + Stun Bolt combo, all of which everyone appreciated, though by then it was too late and Unity, at 1 HP, died instantly to his flipped fury. A first-round play of Natural-Born Vigor made sure the Naturalist could armor himself and attack in the same round, and he played as many ongoings as he could to sacrifice to Iron Douche’s cheap shots. Golem Unity’s death is the only reason the Wraith survived, letting Wraith play two Impromptu Inventions before her turn to get a massive setup in play and then elbow Legacy in the throat to make sure he didn’t inflict any damage that round. In round six it was over, and the Naturalist has cleared all events.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Agent of Gloom in Megalopolis. You’d think that would suck, right? Well, there’s no problem that having a Legacy, even Greatest Legacy, on hand for won’t make at least three times easier; particularly when the rest of the team is Wraith, Setback, and Freedom Tempest. I consider it an insult to your intelligence to describe how it went except to say that Spite’s first played card was a victim card, Legacy’s first was Inspired Presence, and Wraith’s first was Razor Ordinance. At the end of the game, the whole team was only down by 9 HP, and Setback had inflicted most of that on himself with frequent use of Looking Up.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
The Chairman attempts to extend his operations to Megalopolis.  Initial opposition from KNYFE, Redeemer Fanatic, and Dark Visionary is easily crushed.  The heroes regroup, call on Haka as a reinforcement, and reengage the villain before he is ready for them.

With the additional hero the underbosses and thugs are more easily handled, and Haka takes great glee in pounding on the Operative after she retaliates on him repeatedly for Organization thugs being taken out.  The Chairman himself joins the fray after a number of underbosses are removed by KNYFE and Haka's assaults.  (Fanatic is getting chops in, but not quite like KNYFE's combos or Haka.  Dark Visionary is demoralizing the Organization psychically, and also manipulating their plans without their knowledge.)

The Chairman and his Organization are defeated.  It seems he miscalculated about a few things between Megalopolis and Rook City.

1.  The jails are more secure.  (The first Prision Break was played as the first villain card play.  The second discarded later on due to a Wrecking Uppercut by KNYFE.)  So the underbosses never got back out into the fray.

2.  Rook City doesn't have a monorail, but Megalopolis does.  A play of "Rook City Is Mine" brought out *both* Plummeting Monorails.  And they proceeded to plummet onto The Chairman and The Operative for two turns.  This accounted for 20 damage on The Chairman, and at least 10 damage to The Operative.  (Helped on the second turn by Dark Visionary playing Wrest The Mind on one so that one of it's attacks finished off The Operative rather than hitting a hero.)  The Chairman himself went down on the next turn as KNYFE worked him over with a combo and Fanatic finished him off.

(Edit: Well, I messed that up.  The Chairman is immune to environmental damage.  I set things back up and finished him off again since the heroes were able to generate the damage on him before the villain deck recycled.  Was much closer though due to some additional healing and retaliation damage.)

posts.cooked: I think I dislike la Capitan with H=4. All those crew members ripped the team up. Rook City Wraith went down pretty hard, but Bunker, Dark Watch Expatriette, and the Argent Adept did eventually toss her punk ass back into the Time Cataclysm. The Argent Adept was fairly key here, getting Wraith to throw out a Micro-Targeting Computer-enhanced Throwing Knives twice per round (then Expatriette using her Assault Rifle or Pride and Prejudice twice, depending on circumstances), and Bunker was throwing out a fairly steady string of damage with his Grenade Launcher. The most interesting thing to happen is how many of la Capitan’s good cards were buried by her “keep drawing until you get some crew cards” cards. Woo.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Tempest, Wraith, and Nightmist against the Ennead in Silver Gulch. The only interesting thing to happen was Lost in Time getting played the same round heroes flipped Nuit, but a quick scan through the deck after the game indicates it’s impossible for Nuit to end the game that way, so whew. Otherwise, it was just all about spending the first round reducing Nuit to the lowest HP of the group just in case a gunman came out to target low-HP targets (and he did; fortunately, Set had also been whittled down to take fire). In an H=3 game, Wraith’s Smoke Bombs took care of a lot of damage, sooooo…yeah. That was that. Everyone survived fine. The biggest damage to the party may have come from Nightmist spamming Oblivion spells.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Engine of War Bunker, Greatest Legacy, and Price of Freedom Wraith vs. the Matriarch. Heroes won in six rounds, thanks almost surely to Legacy having a Take Down in his opening hand so Bunker could play a Flak Cannon, shoot her mask, shoot it again on Legacy’s turn, and then Wraith could throw knives at people. The heroes ate her psychic retaliation. In round 2, Bunker, now the highest-HP hero, put out armor to immunize the party from further retaliation and finished off her mask, then started shooting the little prat herself on Legacy’s turn when he got out Inspiring Presence. Wraith got out a Micro-Targeting Computer to start tearing up the Matriarch and her Carrion Fields. The party ate a little more HP, and then Wraith got out her Smoke Bombs and a Utility Belt, which was pretty much game over.

Big props go to the fine police of Megalopolis, who did their duty shooting that little skank. If they hadn’t, her final-round play that got her mask back in play would have made round 7 extremely painful.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I thought maybe I got off easy with the Matriarch, so I tried it again. Random rolls bring out Dark Watch Mister Fixer, Legacy, Golem Unity, and Parse.

The only thing anyone ever needs to say to or about the Matriarch is, “Stealth Bot.”

“But I have counterattacks,” she might say.

“And I might care, if I actually had to kill your birds because their damage wasn’t being eaten by Stealth Bot,” you say.

“But sometimes I do direct damage and destroy ongoing cards,” she might say.

“You know what eats damage and isn’t an ongoing card? Stealth Bot,” you would say.

“But–” she might say.

“Stealth Bot,” you will say.

Then she will shut up and you will win the game.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Engine of War Bunker, Expatriette, and Elemental Wrath Absolute Zero took on Iron Legacy in Insula Primalis. As usual, it was just a matter of losing games until I finally started with enough ongoing-destroying cards in hand to have a chance. Probably wouldn’t have been as bad if I had ignored the random roll environment and just picked one less evil, but meh.

I dunno, I really haven’t figured out what’s supposed to be fun about this guy, since the entire strategy seems to be to rely on luck to skunk him right out of the gate or just concede after round two. Maybe if I fight him enough, I’ll figure out the strategy, but so far it seems to be, “Break his toys in the first round or die.”

I had a marathon game against him using Legacy.  Got damage redirection going and Legacy immune to melee damage; which is 90% of Iron Legacy's attacks.  Key from there is Legacy keeping his stuff out to keep the defense up for the heroes and then the other heroes being able to build up and trash Iron Legacy, or at least knock his ongoings out and make him easier to defeat.  (A similar strategy is having a hero incapped early who has an incap power that protects the heroes.)

The other games have been quick losses, or an early ongoing-stripping card play followed by a beatdown.  You just don't tend to get middle-of-the-road games against him.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: KNYFE, Parse, and Setback beat up Baron Blade in the Block. It was shockingly hard, given the only thing KNYFE is good at, but what can you do.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Dark Watch Nightmist, Engine of War Bunker, the Visionary, and Horus versus Skinwalker Gloomweaver on Mars. It was really grueling there at the end, mostly because I gambled badly on Nightmist needing to wipe out a relic and a bunch of voodoo pins with an Oblivion spell enhanced by Imbued Flame…and she drew two 4-point cards. I really need to learn to count cards with her. That knocked everyone down from a comfortable teens to single digit HP, and from there I was quite a bit like a cornered rat, just biting as fast and hard as possible. If it hadn’t been for a very early play of Twist the Ether, with Visionary cynically and gleefully increasing Gloomweaver’s damage against Nightmist (so she could reflect it back at him) and reducing it against all the other heroes, then increasing it when it was time for him to devour his own cards, the team would have lost. Everyone was between 2 and 5 HP in the final round.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Advanced Ambuscade against Dark Watch Mister Fixer, Greatest Legacy, KNYFE, and Tempest in Freedom Plaza was over in about eight rounds, even though Legacy was immunizing the group against projectile damage by round 3. As usual, Mister Fixer was the biggest stumbling point, delaying everyone’s growth with his Bitter Strike. There were three rounds of unmitigated fire damage from his grenade launcher or whatever that card is called, but everything got beat down pretty rapidly.
